steps.tx: The urogenital system arises from **intermediate mesoderm**. Excretory units and gonads both develop from this layer. The kidney develops in three successive stages: **pronephros**, **mesonephros** and **metanephros**. Only the metanephros forms the permanent kidney in humans. The pronephros and most of the mesonephros regress early, while parts of the mesonephros persist as genital structures in males and females.

vis.alt: Flow diagram of kidney development in three stages: pronephros vestigial, mesonephros transient with the mesonephric duct, metanephros permanent with the ureteric bud forming the collecting system and metanephric mesenchyme forming the nephrons.
vis.caption: Ureteric bud makes the collecting system and ureter; metanephric mesenchyme makes the nephron up to the distal tubule.

steps.tx: The **ureteric bud** is an outgrowth from the mesonephric duct near its entry into the cloaca. It gives rise to the ureter, renal pelvis, calyces and collecting tubules. The **metanephric blastema** is the cap of tissue over each bud. It forms the nephrons, including glomeruli, proximal and distal convoluted tubules and loop of Henle. Collecting system from the bud, secretory unit from the blastema.
steps.say: The ureteric bud is an outgrowth from the mesonephric duct near its entry into the cloaca. It gives rise to the ureter, renal pelvis, calyces and collecting tubules. The metanephric blastema is the cap of tissue over each bud. It forms the nephrons, including glomeruli, proximal and distal convoluted tubules and loop of Henle. The collecting system comes from the bud, and the secretory unit comes from the blastema.

rows: Glomeruli, convoluted tubules, loop of Henle

steps.tx: The **mesonephric duct** is the main genital duct in males. It forms the epididymis, ductus deferens, ejaculatory ducts and seminal vesicles. The **paramesonephric duct** is the main genital duct in females. It forms the uterine tubes, uterus and upper vagina. In males it regresses, leaving the appendix of the testis and the prostatic utricle. Lower vagina comes from the urogenital sinus.

steps.tx: The **urogenital sinus** comes from the anterior part of the cloaca after the urorectal septum divides it. It forms the urinary bladder, most of the urethra and the vestibule of the vagina. The **trigone** of the bladder is an exception: it comes from mesoderm, through incorporation of the caudal mesonephric ducts. Urachus, a remnant of allantois, becomes the median umbilical ligament. Incomplete closure may leave a urachal cyst, sinus or fistula.

steps.tx: Testes develop near the kidneys and descend later. The **gubernaculum** is a mesenchymal cord attached to the caudal pole of the gonad. The **processus vaginalis** is a peritoneal evagination that follows the gubernaculum into the scrotal swelling. Testes reach the inguinal region around 12 weeks, and enter the scrotum late in fetal life. In the female, the gubernaculum forms the ovarian and round ligaments.

vis.alt: Flow diagram of testicular descent: gubernaculum anchors the caudal pole, processus vaginalis evaginates the abdominal wall, testis passes through the inguinal canal and reaches the scrotum; persistence of the process gives indirect hernia or hydrocele, failure to descend gives cryptorchidism.
vis.caption: Failed descent: cryptorchidism. Persistent processus vaginalis: indirect hernia or hydrocele.

steps.tx: Fusion of the caudal poles of the two kidneys produces a **horseshoe kidney**. The fused mass is stopped from ascending by the inferior mesenteric artery. Renal agenesis is due to defective ureteric bud or metanephric tissue, and the adrenal gland stays in its normal position. In the uterus, a **bicornuate uterus** follows failed fusion of the paramesonephric ducts. Hypospadias results from incomplete fusion of the urethral folds on the genital tubercle.

vis.alt: Table of renal anomalies with cause: horseshoe kidney fused at lower poles and trapped under the inferior mesenteric artery, pelvic kidney from failed ascent, renal agenesis from absent ureteric bud, and Potter sequence from bilateral agenesis.
vis.caption: Horseshoe kidney: lower poles fuse and ascent stops at the inferior mesenteric artery.
